# ST0002 Design -- the second-fleet rollout

Eight projects, two shapes of work, one protocol per shape. ST0001's design decisions (D1-D24, `intent/st/COMPLETED/ST0001/design.md`) and the migration guide (`docs/migration.md`) remain the base; this file records only what is NEW about this fleet and the per-project rulings the survey forced. An executing session should be able to run any WP from this file, the WP's info.md, and acceptance.md, with no other context.

## The survey (2026-08-10, read-only)

| Project          | Lang         | Last       | Dev launcher                           | Tests                | Pre-commit hook             | Notes                                              |
| ---------------- | ------------ | ---------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| Multiplyer       | elixir       | 2026-06-25 | none                                   | test/ (ExUnit)       | intent chain                | pins elixir 1.18.0 / erlang 27.0 (oldest anywhere) |
| Arca/arca_config | elixir       | 2026-08-04 | none                                   | test/ (ExUnit)       | intent chain                | published library; upstream of arca_cli            |
| Arca/arca_cli    | elixir       | 2026-08-04 | none                                   | test/ (ExUnit)       | intent chain                | deps on arca_config via github branch main         |
| MicroGPTEx       | elixir       | 2026-06-25 | none                                   | test/ (ExUnit)       | intent chain + raw prettier | DONE (WP-04): a paper; docs/bin/publish builds it  |
| Molt             | shell        | 2026-06-25 | bin/molt (179) + bootstrap.sh (153)    | test/*.bats          | intent chain + raw prettier | real migration, small                              |
| Utilz            | shell        | 2026-08-06 | bin/ is the PRODUCT: 14 tools + utilz  | none found (depth 2) | intent chain                | install beside the product; name collision         |
| Pplr             | shell        | 2025-07-19 | bin/pplr (70) + 20 pplr_* satellites   | tests/*.bats         | RAW prettier --write on .md | oldest; Icon cruft in bin/; templates/ dirt parked |
| Prolix           | elixir+swift | 2026-06-25 | none                                   | test/ (ExUnit)       | intent chain + raw prettier | Dockerfile + fly.toml; xcodeproj at native/ios     |

Dirt at survey: Multiplyer `_Archive/web/priv/static/images/icons/` untracked, Pplr `templates/icons/` untracked. Both parked -- surfaced to hv, never silently fixed or silently carried into an install commit.

**hv's review (2026-08-10) parked two of the eight.** Pplr: to be redone as a Rust project at some point; migrating the current shell fleet is not right for it. Utilz: the beside-the-product shape needs more thought. The survey rows above stay as the record for when either returns; WP-06 and WP-07 carry the rulings and no ACs. **Then hv's Fable review CANCELLED a third, the same day: Multiplyer is EOL.** It is retired rather than migrated -- moved to `_Archive`, with the parts worth keeping extracted into a net-new project, **Riffle**, built with Intent and devbin from the outset. Devbin is never installed into it. WP-01 carries the ruling and no ACs.

**Then hv cancelled a fourth, 2026-08-10: no devbin for Molt.** The WP halted at its own inventory, having found that `bin/molt` is the PRODUCT -- symlinked into `~/bin` on every machine hv owns -- and that `bin/bootstrap.sh` is a public `curl` installer. That made Molt the beside-the-product shape already parked at WP-06, not the easy migration the survey recorded; hv ruled it out of scope rather than reshaped. WP-05 carries the ruling, the eleven dispositions and the collision probe.

The thread's scope is the remaining FOUR: arca_config, arca_cli, MicroGPTEx, Prolix. Three are done; **Prolix is the only work left in this thread.**

**What went with Multiplyer is worth naming: the deps-drift protocol's hardest planned test.** It was proven at WP-04 on the gentlest possible ground -- a baseline already green -- and Multiplyer was to stress it against the oldest pins in either fleet over 122 lib files on Ash, igniter, ecto and instructor. No remaining WP replaces that. The protocol's SHAPE is proven; its STRENGTH is not, and nothing in this thread should later read as though it were.

## The two paths

**CORRECTED AT WP-02, AND THE CORRECTION INVERTS THIS SECTION.** As surveyed: five fresh installs, one migration. As built, after two cancellations: **ONE fresh install (MicroGPTEx, done) and THREE migrations.** The survey looked for the un-migrated shape it knew -- `bin/<prj>` beside `bin/<prj>_helpers`, which is what the first fleet had -- and hv's OLDER convention puts the same launcher in `scripts/`. Four of the six carry one, and none of the first fleet does, which is why the pattern never came up in ST0001:

| Project    | scripts/                                                                        | Lines |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- |
| arca_config | cli, iex, test (+ a gh/ dir)                                                    | 16    |
| arca_cli    | cli, completions, iex, mcduct, repl, test, update_completions, wrap-up (+ gh/)  | 220   |
| Multiplyer  | build, cli, completions, debug, echo, iex, mcduct, mix, repl, server, taillog, test, ta_test_wrapper | 179   |
| Prolix      | cli, completions, dbproxy, echo, flysql, iex, mcduct, mix, repl, server, taillog, test | 235   |
| MicroGPTEx  | (none -- genuinely a fresh install, and it was)                                 | --    |
| Molt        | (none -- and `bin/molt` is the PRODUCT, not a launcher: WP-05, cancelled)       | --    |

hv, 2026-08-10: "the scripts/ dir is my old way of doing scripts in a project (pre devbin) and needs cleaning up, too" -- so the deletion is sanctioned, at the protocol's usual place (last, after equivalence).

These are small migrations, not Conflab-sized: ~471 lines across three projects, of which 471 minus arca_config's 16 is two projects' worth. But each one is a MIGRATION and gets the migration protocol, not the fresh-install one. (This sentence used to read "Molt-sized", using Molt as the unit of a small migration. Molt was never a migration at all.)

**Standing dispositions, so the WPs that meet these do not re-litigate them:**

- **`scripts/mcduct` -- DELETE, do not port.** hv, 2026-08-10: "that can just be binned, it's not used any more." It appears in arca_cli, Multiplyer and Prolix, byte-identical in the latter two and divergent in arca_cli, so it was also a Highlander breach at fleet scale -- but the disposition makes that moot. It goes with the rest of `scripts/`; no devbin command, no help topic, no equivalence row beyond recording that it was retired unported.
- **`scripts/` itself -- DELETE, at the protocol's usual place.** hv, 2026-08-10: "my old way of doing scripts in a project (pre devbin) and needs cleaning up, too." Last, after equivalence is proven through the new entry point, in its own commit, with the CALLERS followed -- arca_config's deletion also moved README, a moduledoc and a test comment.
- **A script whose behaviour the framework already provides does not become a command.** arca_config's three collapsed to one config line plus an existing flag: the `.env` preamble in all three was already done by `config/dotenv.exs`, and `scripts/iex` was the `cli` command under `--iex` (D20). Ask what the TARGET already does before porting what the source did.

**Fresh install** (one: MicroGPTEx -- DONE). No existing dev launcher, so no inventory, no equivalence pack, no switch day. Fence -> `devbin install` alongside -> `doctor` green + `help --why` read -> ONE install commit -> config, handlers and authored help in their own commits -> gates green through `bin/devbin`.

**Migrate** (three, after Multiplyer's and Molt's cancellations: arca_config, arca_cli, Prolix). The full ST0001 WP-10/11 protocol: inventory the old launcher with a disposition for every command, ACs before code, install alongside, prove equivalence command-by-command in a pack, switch on hv's explicit go, delete last in its own commit. Live projects, no git branches (ST0001 D10); rollback is one revert.

**The inventory step is not a formality, and Molt is the proof.** In the two arca projects it merely re-sized a WP written as a fresh install. At Molt it was the only thing standing between the WP's own deliverables ("old launcher deleted last") and deleting the product. It is first for a reason: **it is the step where a WP is allowed to discover it should not run.**

**The general form, which is the third survey error of this thread and the same one every time: a survey finds the shape it is looking for.** ST0001's own lesson was that a shape search finds the right shape and the wrong kind (it matched Intent). This is the mirror -- the right kind, missed for having the wrong shape. Ask what the thing DOES (is there a dev launcher?) before asking where it lives.

**The fourth error, at Molt, is the sharpest, because the survey already HELD the concept that would have caught it.** It classified Utilz correctly -- the WP-06 row below records that `bin/utilz` is the PRODUCT and that devbin must enter beside it. Then it looked at `bin/molt` (179) + `bin/bootstrap.sh` (153) and wrote "real migration, small". Same shape, same fleet, same survey, opposite conclusion -- because the Utilz row was reasoned from what the files DO and the Molt row was reasoned from how many lines they have. **Having the right concept is not the same as applying it; a survey applies it only where it happens to look.** The correction is not a better heuristic, it is a cheaper habit: open the file. Twenty lines of `bin/molt` name it a product CLI.

**The fence comes first in both paths.** `bin/.devbin/lib/` lands in `.prettierignore` (append, never assume-create: list the file first) BEFORE the install commit, per the step now in `docs/migration.md`.

**Corrected at WP-04: the survey's "intent chain" column was the wrong half of the answer.** Intent's chained hook runs CRITICS, not a Markdown pass -- it is not the issue-0008 hazard and never was. The hazard is the project's OWN `prettier --write` step sitting after the chain block, and only three of the six have one: **MicroGPTEx, Molt and Prolix**. Multiplyer, arca_config and arca_cli chain to Intent and stop. The fence still lands in all six (a hand `prettier` run or an editor plugin is the other blast radius -- Lamplight's fence comment says "on every path"), but in three of them it is load-bearing at commit time and in three it is insurance. **Read the hook, not the survey row.**

WP-04 proved the fence rather than assuming it, and that is the pattern for Molt and Prolix: stage a deliberately unstable probe `.md` under `bin/.devbin/lib/`, run the hook, watch it get rewritten; add the fence, watch it come back byte-identical; stage a project `.md` alongside to prove the fence is selective and not a blanket disable. One disproved risk worth not re-deriving: when EVERY staged `.md` is ignored, prettier skips silently at rc 0, so a `set -euo pipefail` hook does not abort a commit that stages only vendored Markdown.

## The languages ruling (settled at WP-04; every remaining WP consumes it)

**devbin's `project.languages` is GATE SCOPE. Intent's `languages` is project composition. They are two different facts that happen to share a name, and mirroring one into the other is a defect.**

The first fleet is unanimous and nobody wrote it down. Conflab: Intent `[shell, elixir, lua, rust, swift]` -> devbin `[elixir, rust, swift]`. Laksa: `[shell, elixir]` -> `[elixir]`. Baize: `[elixir, swift, rust, shell]` -> `[elixir, shell]`. Lamplight: seven -> `[elixir, rust, lua]`. Baize keeps shell because it has a real bats suite over its vendored lib; Laksa drops it because it has none. The question devbin's list answers is **"which gate arms does this project have something behind?"**, not "what is this project written in".

Get it backwards and the damage is immediate and quiet: declaring a language lights up its catalogue rows -- `test.shell` wants `bats tests`, `check.format` grows an arm -- with nothing behind them, and the promotions ruling then turns a zero-work run into a FAILED gate. A red gate that is red because of a config line nobody meant is worse than no gate.

Corroboration from the as-built: `check critic` iterates INTENT's language list, not devbin's, because the critic library is Intent's and the rules are about the source. Both lists are right at once, for different consumers.

**This retires the reason WP-04 was originally given.** The plan justified MicroGPTEx's `[elixir]` by the project's 2026-06-25 commit that "dropped lua" -- but that commit's own message says *"Baseline restored to elixir + shell"*, so Intent declares shell there to this day. The conclusion was right and the reason was wrong, which is the dangerous combination: applied to Multiplyer, arca_cli or Prolix, "mirror Intent's list" would have declared gates that do not exist. Read what the project HAS A GATE FOR, and record the reason at the key.

## The deps-drift protocol (elixir; WP-04 proves it first -- hv's re-order of 2026-08-10 -- and WP-01/02/03/08 reuse it, with WP-01 as its hardest test)

Order matters, and the sealed gates are the record:

1. **Toolchain before anything.** `bin/devbin check toolchain` right after install. A project whose pinned or implied toolchain no longer exists on this machine cannot even baseline; bumping pins happens on record, as its own commit, before deps are touched.

   **Amended at WP-04: step 1 has a precondition the protocol did not state.** `check toolchain` DIES without a `.tool-versions` (`lib/cmd/check:230`), and only Multiplyer has one. That refusal is correct -- you reach the arm only by declaring it, so "compare the pins" with no pins is a real error, not the determinate-fact shape the no-Dockerfile arm reports -- but it means step 1 cannot run until the pin file exists.

   **Amended AGAIN at WP-02, correcting the amendment above.** WP-04 recorded hv's call as "these projects DO get one". That over-generalised a decision taken about a project with no CI and no other home for the fact, and arca_config proved it wrong within the day: its CI runs a three-cell matrix (OTP 27/1.18.0, 28/1.18.4, 29/1.20.2) whose header records why the top cell exists, so a pin file there would be a SECOND home, hand-kept in step, and would not even agree -- the matrix tops out at 1.20.2 and the machine runs 1.20.3.

   **BOTH AMENDMENTS ABOVE ARE SUPERSEDED. hv, 2026-08-10, at WP-03: there is ONE shape.** Every project gets a `.tool-versions` at the fleet's current pins, CI reads it, and the arm is live. Stale or implied toolchain pins are not to be left anywhere, and everything that can be on the latest is.

   - **The "three shapes" rule was mine, not hv's, and it was wrong.** hv's actual policy has been written down since 2026-07-28, in Baize's own `.tool-versions` header: *"run the latest, and keep this file matching what you actually run. When they disagree, local and CI compile with different compilers and the only type gate we have stops being one gate."* It is fleet-wide and it is not a per-project judgement call. I had the evidence in the corpus and derived a different rule from one project's CI layout.
   - **The middle shape was wrong on its own facts, too.** arca_config's matrix was supposed to own the pin; its top cell said 1.20.2 while every local run used 1.20.3, and the comment above it still claimed the cell tracked local. The fact it "already had a home" for had silently drifted, which is the argument for a gate rather than against one. arca_cli was worse: CI hardcoded 1.18/OTP 27, two majors behind every local run, with `--warnings-as-errors` as the project's only type gate.
   - **A CI matrix is not a competing home; it answers a different question.** The pin file is the version a project is DEVELOPED on. A matrix's older cells are the versions it still SUPPORTS -- worth keeping for a published library, floored at what `mix.exs` requires. Two facts, one home each. Only a cell that CLAIMS to track local is a copy, and that copy gets guarded: arca_config's CI now hard-fails when its top cell disagrees with the pin file, because GitHub expands a matrix before any step runs and the literal cannot be avoided.
   - **Where a project's `mix.exs` requirement is looser than a pin**, the pin is the tighter statement and the file should say so.

   The general lesson, and it is the second instance of it in one day: **hv's call about project A is not a fleet ruling, and a fleet ruling that already exists is not mine to re-derive.** Both errors came from reasoning forward from one project instead of reading what the corpus already recorded -- Baize's file had the answer the whole time.

   **The general form: hv's call about project A is not a fleet ruling, and writing it up as one is how a good decision becomes a bad default.** Ask what was true about the project the call was made for.
2. **Baseline BEFORE update.** `mix deps.get` then `bin/devbin test all` -- possibly red, and recorded red. The point is separating pre-existing drift from update-caused breakage; a baseline nobody recorded turns every later failure into an argument.
3. **`mix deps.update --all`, then resolve**: lockfile conflicts, deprecations, compile warnings, test failures. Ordinary work; the before/after seals are the evidence.
4. **Green through the new entry point**, then the lockfile and fixes land in their own commits, never inside the install commit.

hv sanctioned full-suite runs on these eight as part of drift resolution (2026-08-10, in-conversation). The Lamplight full-mix prohibition does not extend here. The another-writer doctrine does: `ps` before any purge-style operation, quiesce before anything destructive.

## Per-project rulings the survey forced

- **Utilz (WP-06) -- PARKED, hv 2026-08-10: needs more thought.** What the survey established, kept for when it returns: `bin/utilz` is the PRODUCT, not a dev launcher -- fourteen shipped tools and their dispatcher live in `bin/`, so devbin would enter as dev tooling beside them, with no `bin/utilz` symlink, and the WP would open by proving that `devbin install` against an existing non-devbin `bin/utilz` refuses rather than clobbers.
- **Pplr (WP-07) -- PARKED, hv 2026-08-10: to be redone as a Rust project; this migration is not right for it.** What the survey established, kept for the rewrite's benefit: `bin/pplr` (70 lines) dispatches to twenty `pplr_*` satellites (natural handler candidates, several colliding with builtin names); the pre-commit hook runs RAW `prettier --write` on staged Markdown; `bin/` carries a macOS `Icon` file (the `Icon\r` glob hazard); untracked `templates/icons/` dirt; oldest tree of the eight (2025-07).
- **Prolix (WP-08): three firsts.** First live swift declaration -- the catalogue's `test.swift` / `fmt.swift` rows have never met a real project, and the xcodeproj lives at `native/ios/Prolix.xcodeproj` with no root `Package.swift`, so the xcodebuild command lines need config overrides; treat whatever the builtin rows get wrong as base findings, not local hacks. First second-fleet deploy target: `Dockerfile` + `fly.toml` means the `check toolchain` image arm is live here from day one. No root `.tool-versions` -- adding one is surfaced to hv, never silent.
- **Arca pair (WP-02 strictly before WP-03) -- and both before WP-01.** `arca_cli` depends on `arca_config` via a GitHub branch dep (`branch: "main"`, `override: true`): config is upstream, goes first, and cli's `deps.update` then follows it. Both are published libraries, two days quiet; drift risk low, semver discipline high -- a resolve that would move a public API is hv's call, not the agent's. **Multiplyer branch-deps on BOTH of them** (plus `arca_dbutils`, which this thread does not touch), so the pair is upstream of the thread's hardest WP too -- see the sequencing note below.
- **MicroGPTEx (WP-04) -- DONE, 2026-08-10.** Record: `intent/st/ST0002/WP/04/microgptex-install.md`. Six commits, `b7cefc3`..`820da68`. It is a PAPER and the small implementation it describes -- one module, one test file, two dev-only deps, no `bin/` at all, no application, no database, no CI -- so `docs/bin/publish` (mdagg + pandoc + typst) is the build artefact and `docs publish` is the point of the install, not a nicety. ex_doc is a dependency and is NOT the doc build; reading rather than assuming was the whole value of that instruction. devbin declares `[elixir]` per the languages ruling above. Five built-ins switched off (`server`, `cli`, `repl`, `db`, `build`), each with its reason at the key: the test is whether a command is RUNNABLE, not whether it resolves.
- **~~Multiplyer (WP-01) goes first deliberately.~~ CANCELLED 2026-08-10 -- Multiplyer is EOL.** The reasoning is kept because it explains what the thread lost: an ordinary elixir project with certain drift, where the deps protocol would have been proven against real drift on a simple project. Nothing replaces it.
- **Toolchain pins fleet-wide -- EVERY project gets one, at the current pins** (hv, 2026-08-10; the standing policy since 2026-07-28). The fleet's pins are `erlang 29.0.5` / `elixir 1.20.3-otp-29`, which is what this machine runs. Done: MicroGPTEx, arca_config, arca_cli, plus the whole first fleet. Prolix gets its own at WP-08; Molt is out of scope and never gets one from this thread. "No pin file" is no longer a reportable state for an elixir project here; it is a gap to close.

  Multiplyer's pin was called out here as the most dangerous of the lot -- the only second-fleet project that HAD one, reading `elixir 1.18.0` / `erlang 27.0`, two majors stale, so the gate would read it and report agreement with a toolchain nobody runs. **It was bumped (Multiplyer `c8a7a51b`) before the cancellation landed, and that commit is now history in a repository being archived.** The lesson stands even though the project does not: a stale pin is worse than an absent one, because an absent one cannot lie.

## What stays behind hv's explicit go

The switch day; every deletion of an existing launcher; any pin bump that changes a published library's support surface; anything destructive in a tree that may have another writer. Everything else inside a WP is the executing agent's to run, including full suites on these four.

**Added 2026-08-10, from WP-03: publishing is hv's too.** AC-03.2 needs arca_cli's `arca_config` GitHub dep to resolve to post-WP-02 upstream, and it cannot until arca_config's ten WP-02 commits are pushed. A push is outward-facing and does not become the agent's merely because a WP is blocked on it.

## Sequencing rationale

Simplest first, per hv (2026-08-10): MicroGPTEx opens the thread and proves the deps protocol on the gentlest ground. Molt is the thread's one migration and proves the shell shape. Prolix closes, carrying every novelty at once -- swift arms, deploy image, iOS layout -- on top of a by-then boring elixir path.

**Overtaken by events, 2026-08-10, and the shell shape is the casualty.** Molt is cancelled, so the thread never proves the shell shape at all: Prolix now carries the first live swift arms AND the deploy-image arm AND its own migration, with no shell precedent ahead of it and no easy predecessor to have de-risked anything. Every project this thread still touches is an elixir one. **`shell` and `swift` gate scope reaches WP-08 unexercised** -- which is a fact about WP-08's risk, not a reason to reopen anything.

**Amended the same day, on hv's call, and the amendment is the more interesting half.** Multiplyer was to follow MicroGPTEx as the protocol's hardest test; reading its `mix.exs` at WP start showed it branch-deps on `arca_config` and `arca_cli` at `main` with `override: true`. The two WPs queued BEHIND it were its upstream. Running it first would have resolved the thread's hardest dependency graph against today's arca main and then moved it again, silently, when WP-02/03 committed to those repos -- a second resolution nobody would record, because WP-01 would already be closed. So: arca_config, arca_cli, then Multiplyer, which resolves once against a settled upstream.

**The general form is worth more than the fix: dependency direction is not visible in the survey table.** The survey recorded "deps on arca_config via github branch main" against arca_cli's row and stopped there, because it was reading each project as a candidate rather than reading the fleet as a graph. Before sequencing a rollout across projects that depend on each other, read every `mix.exs` for intra-fleet deps FIRST -- the ordering constraint lives in the dependency edges, not in how hard each project looks on its own.
